_comment: Mutation testing: breaks the source on purpose and checks the tests notice.
A mutant that leaves the suite green is a bug the tests cannot see — unlike line
coverage, this cannot be satisfied by executing code without asserting on it.
Two rules keep it usable:
1. NEVER gate a PR on this. A run re-executes the suite once per mutant. It belongs on
a nightly schedule or in front of a refactor — see the `mutation` job in ci.yml.
2. Keep `mutate` pointed at logic. Generated code (contracts/, tests/mocks/generated.ts),
config and view templates produce noise exclusively.
Thresholds come from a real run, not from a number invented in advance. Raise
`break` when the score rises; never lower it to make a run pass.
Measured 2026-08-08: 81.11% total / 83.96% of covered code, 826 mutants, 3m43s (that run
shared the machine with the backend's; alone it is ~90s). `break` sits below that on
purpose — it catches a real regression, not normal drift.
Unchanged from 81.04% / 84.04% over 786 mutants on 2026-08-06, which is the right answer:
that window added tests and configuration, and no source logic, so a moved score would have
been the thing to explain.
middlewares/authentications.ts (59.09%) is the weakest file here AND the one that
`coverage.thresholds.perFile` exposed in vitest.config.ts — two instruments, independently,
naming the same file. It is the guard layer, so it is also the most valuable to finish.
Expect ±1 point of run-to-run noise, all of it in plugins/http/index.ts: several of its
refresh-interceptor mutants hang rather than fail, and whether one is recorded as a
timeout (which counts as killed) or as a survivor depends on how loaded the machine is.
Judge a drop against that band before treating it as a regression.
Still worth attention, in rough order of payoff: plugins/http/index.ts (64.80%),
middlewares/authentications.ts (59.09%), and the products/users/orders stores (~65%
each, the same three read/write paths in each file).
History, because both numbers are instructive:
- An earlier run scored 55.95%/65.98% over 435 mutants. It is what produced
tests/unit/utils/formatters.spec.ts: formatters.ts scored 0% because no test called
it at all, and coverage reports had never said so (vitest.config.ts now sets
`coverage.include`, which is the cheap way to see that class of gap).
- A later run scored 55.74% over 784 mutants, with 182 of the 318 survivors in the
single file responseSchemaMap.ts. That file is a 52-row lookup table, and it had
been tested by sampling a handful of rows. Replacing the sample with a table-driven
test over every row — plus deeper-path, prefixed-path and empty-segment negatives
per row, which target the two anchors and the `[^/]+` quantifier — took it to 100%
and the suite as a whole from 55.74% to 81.12%. Sampling a declarative table is
the failure mode to watch for here.
── SCOPE, and why the score dropped on purpose (stage 1 of the widening) ────────────────
`mutate` covers every `.ts` under stores, router, features (stores, schemas, routes,
composables, realtime), middlewares, plugins/http and utils. It used to be four globs over
the best-tested slice of the repo, which meant everything outside was not merely unmeasured
but INVISIBLE: a file absent from the report reads exactly like a file with no survivors.
Widening lowers the headline number, and that is the deliverable rather than a regression.
The gap between `mutationScore` and `mutationScoreBasedOnCoveredCode` is the size of the
untested surface, stated as a number for the first time. Compare per-FILE against
`mutation-baseline.json`; the total is a ratio over a population that just changed and is not
comparable to the pre-widening figure.
`.vue` is deliberately NOT here yet. Stryker CAN mutate an SFC — it maps the file to the HTML
parser and mutates the `<script>` block — but it does NOT mutate template expressions, so
including SFCs would report a number that implies template coverage nobody has. It is
sequenced after component tests exist (plan §5.4/§5.6 stage 5), or the report is unreadable
noise.
`utils/i18n.ts` stays excluded: it is configuration of the i18n runtime, and its mutants are
about vue-i18n's behaviour rather than this app's.
The rule is that `break` rises when a score sustains a higher band and is NEVER lowered to
make a run pass. The one sanctioned exception is a change to `mutate`, in the same commit as
that change, recording both numbers and the reason — which is this.
before the widening:  81.11% total / 83.96% covered,   826 mutants  (four globs)
after the widening:   59.82% total / 79.45% covered, 1346 mutants  (the list above)
Those are not two measurements of the same thing. The POPULATION changed: 520 mutants that
did not exist before are now counted, 332 of them with no test coverage at all. Note that the
covered-code figure barely moved (83.96 -> 79.45) — the assertions did not weaken, the
denominator grew to include code nobody had measured.
THE GAP IS THE DELIVERABLE. 59.82 against 79.45 is the size of the untested surface, stated
as a number for the first time. Where it lives, worst first:
stores/observability.ts   1.42% (131 mutants with no coverage)
stores/profile.ts         6.25% ( 74 no coverage) — it HAS a spec; the spec covers little
features/admin            0.00% ( 30 no coverage) — useAdminObservability.ts
features/realtime        24.56% ( 37 no coverage)
router/index.ts          55.21%
`break` moved 70 -> 50: below the new measurement, so it still answers 'has something
collapsed' rather than 'did the number move'. It is NOT the main gate any more — per-file
regressions are caught by `mutation-baseline.json` via `npm run test:mutation:check`, which is
what makes a single weak file visible instead of averaged away. Raise this band when the score
sustains a higher one, which is a consequence of writing the missing tests rather than a
target to aim at.
8, raised from 4 on 2026-08-09. Stryker runs each worker as a separate PROCESS, and in this
repo each one carries a full test runner (and, in the backend, its own in-memory mongod), so
the ceiling is memory rather than cores. 8 on a 32-core / 30 GB machine leaves headroom deliberately; a laptop
with 8 GB should lower it. It is the cheapest speed-up available and it changes no measurement:
the same mutants are run, just more of them at once.
This value is for a DEVELOPER MACHINE. CI overrides it: `mutation.yml` passes
`--concurrency 3`, because a standard GitHub-hosted runner is 4 vCPU / 16 GB and 12 workers
there would thrash or run out of memory. The safe number is a property of the machine, not
of the project, which is why it is not the same in both places.
Why 8 and not 30-odd: the ceiling here is MEMORY and responsiveness, not cores. Each worker is
a separate process carrying a full test runner and its own in-memory mongod, and the machine is
in use while a run happens — a setting that saturates it is worse than one that finishes a few
minutes later. Measured at 12: free RAM fell to ~6 GB and load average hit 14. Treat 8 as the
resting value and lower it on a smaller machine rather than raising it on a bigger one.
